### Dominion Energy Supports Nonprofits Across the Palmetto State


11/23/2026


[Download this Press Release (opens in new window) PDF 510 KB](https://s205.q4cdn.com/611413639/files/doc_news/2026/11/Dominion-Energy-Supports-Nonprofits-Across-the-Palmetto-State.pdf)


**CAYCE, S.C. (Nov. 23, 2026)** – The Dominion Energy Charitable Foundation is investing nearly $1 million in South Carolina communities during its fall grant cycle, supporting more than 100 nonprofit organizations across the state.


The shareholder-funded grants support a variety of programs and services, including access to essential medications, resources that strengthen rural communities and educational opportunities for students.


“The holidays are a special time to reflect on what it means to give back,” said Keller Kissam, president of Dominion Energy South Carolina. “But for these nonprofits, giving back isn't something they do just once a year. It's the work they do every day to care for our neighbors, strengthen our communities and make our state a better place. We're proud to support and stand alongside them.”


Grant recipients include:


- **Welvista – Columbia, S.C.** – Welvista's Medication Assistance Pharmacy (MAP) provides free prescription medications to eligible uninsured South Carolinians. Based in Columbia and serving residents statewide, MAP delivers medications directly to patients' homes, helping individuals manage chronic conditions and overcome financial barriers to essential healthcare.
- **Lowcountry Community Resource Center – Walterboro, S.C.** – The Community Resource Hub is a year-round initiative connecting residents of Colleton County and surrounding rural communities with educational opportunities, small business support, cultural activities and other resources designed to strengthen community connections and expand access to opportunity.
- **The Green Heart Project – Charleston, S.C.** – The organization's Farm to School Program uses school gardens and hands-on learning to teach students about healthy eating, environmental stewardship and sustainable agriculture.


Funding is available to organizations in areas where Dominion Energy provides electricity, natural gas or has significant business interests. These include Virginia, South Carolina, northeastern North Carolina, and parts of West Virginia, Connecticut and Rhode Island.


Applications for the next round of grants will be accepted from Jan. 11 through Feb. 19, 2027. For more information about the Dominion Energy Charitable Foundation and future grant opportunities, visit[DominionEnergy.com/foundation](http://dominionenergy.com/foundation) .


**About Dominion Energy**


Dominion Energy (NYSE:[D](https://investors.dominionenergy.com/home/default.aspx) ) provides regulated electricity service to 3.6 million homes and businesses in Virginia, North Carolina, and South Carolina, and regulated natural gas service to 500,000 customers in South Carolina; is one of the nation’s leading developers and operators of regulated offshore wind and solar power; and is the largest producer of carbon-free electricity in New England. Through the[Dominion Energy Charitable Foundation](https://www.dominionenergy.com/foundation) , as well as[EnergyShare](https://www.dominionenergy.com/virginia/billing/billing-options-and-assistance/energyshare) and other programs, Dominion Energy contributed more than $40 million in 2025 to community causes. The Foundation supports nonprofit causes that meet basic human needs, protect the environment, promote education, and encourage community vitality. Please visit[DominionEnergy.com](http://www.dominionenergy.com/) to learn more.
